title: Elevated Zero Maze for Animal Behavior Testing
author: Taryn E McFadden

steps.title: Acclimate Animals in Testing Room
steps.instruction: If animals are not normally housed adjacent to the testing room, place their home cages inside the testing room and allow them to acclimate for 30–60 minutes before testing. Keep noise and disturbance to a minimum; do not talk or perform other activities, position wall shields to block the animal’s view of the room, and hang a “Do Not Disturb/Enter” sign on the outermost door.

steps.title: Prepare Environment and Recording Equipment
steps.instruction: Hang the “Testing in Progress – Do Not Enter” sign on the testing‑room door. Verify that the maze is aligned with the floor markings and that the enclosure is correctly positioned to limit external distractions. Plug in and power on the Logitech camera, then log into the computer with PSH credentials. Launch the Logitech recording software and set the parameters to Auto‑flicker = 50 Hz and Field of view = 78°. Note that the maze will appear inverted in the video; later software updates may allow image flipping.

substeps.instruction: Place the “Testing in Progress – Do Not Enter” sign on the door.
Align maze with floor markings and install enclosure.
Plug in and turn on the Logitech camera.
Power on the computer and log in using PSH credentials.
Open Logitech recording software.
Set Auto‑flicker to 50 Hz and Field of view to 78°.

steps.title: Clean Walkway Between and After Tests
steps.instruction: Between subjects, wipe the walkway with a wet paper towel and then dry it. After all testing is completed, clean the walkway with 70 % ethanol; do not use any other disinfectants because they may damage the stage.

steps.title: Start Recording and Place Animal
steps.instruction: Initiate video recording before the animal enters the maze. While holding the animal, press “Start Record” in the software; the camera will begin its countdown, then gently place the animal into the Zero Maze.

substeps.instruction: Initiate recording before animal placement.
Press “Start Record” while holding the animal.
Allow camera countdown to finish.
Place the animal into the maze.

steps.title: Record Behavior and Note Incidents
steps.instruction: Remove a single animal from its home cage using your preferred handling technique, then place it into the maze (standardized or randomized placement as defined by your experimental design). Record behavior for a minimum of 10 minutes while remaining completely silent. If the animal jumps or falls, record the incident in the log (jumps are rare but possible).

substeps.instruction: Remove animal from home cage with chosen handling method.
Place animal into the maze (standardized or randomized).
Record continuously for at least 10 minutes.
Stay silent throughout the test.
Document any jumps or falls.

steps.title: Save, Transfer, and Rename Video Files
steps.instruction: After recording, video files are saved automatically to the local C: drive. Transfer the files to the network drive for processing, rename each file to include animal ID, date, and timepoint, and record the exact start time for each rat on a data sheet to avoid timing errors.

substeps.instruction: Locate video files on the C: drive.
Copy files to the network drive.
Rename files with animal ID, date, and timepoint.
Enter the start time for each rat on a data sheet.

steps.title: Process Video Data in EthoVision
steps.instruction: Open the videos in EthoVision and define four zones: Open Quadrant 1, Open Quadrant 2, Closed Quadrant 1, and Closed Quadrant 2. Group the open zones into an “Open” category and the closed zones into a “Closed” category to extract total time spent in each. Manually verify zone transitions because EthoVision may misclassify them, especially when the animal is in a hidden or transitional area. Optionally enable automatic detection of additional behaviors such as rearing or freezing, but confirm these detections manually.

substeps.instruction: Define Open Quadrant 1, Open Quadrant 2, Closed Quadrant 1, Closed Quadrant 2.
Group zones into “Open” and “Closed” categories.
Extract total time spent in open vs. closed quadrants.
Manually verify transitions to correct misclassifications.
Optionally enable automatic scoring of rearing, freezing, etc., and verify manually.
